match_id: TUCHEL: “I'M NOT SUPER HAPPY!”  England_New Zealand  World Cup warm-up_2026-06-06_EACTE28F-Yc
speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Thomas. Yeah. Happy with that? I'm okay with it.  I'm not super happy about it. I like the second  
half more than the first half. I think we had  more bite in the second half, were more aggressive  
on and off the ball, created a bit more good  half-chances and some good penetrations into the  
box. We played more from our positions and that's  why we played with more speed. And off the ball,  
like I said, we played with a bit more bite. In  the first half, we were out of positions and it  
was a bit too much freestyle, and that slowed our  game down and made it difficult for counter-press,  
because we were not in the positions that we  wanted to be when we started attacking. So that's  
basically the story of the match. I mean, to put  it in context, a lot of our players played last  
time together in November, so it's half a year  ago, and we had four training sessions together.  
Then we mixed the team up completely, so I think  we never played before in these combinations,  
in these formations, to give everyone 45 minutes.  Then you have the conditions, you have the pitch,  
then it can look like this. In terms of the heat,  it was really hot out there. How do you feel they  
are acclimatising? Well, we didn't have a lot of  exposure to the sun because we had three days in  
the rain and grey skies. So we had one training  session in the sun and now this match felt really,  
really hot. But it's good that we're exposed  because that's why we're here. We wanted it  
that way and we need to get used to it because  it will come at some point. When you say a bit  
too much freestyle in the first half, what do  you mean? Position-wise, I think it was not so  
clear. We couldn't translate it so clearly on  the pitch, our positions and when to start the  
attack. On the right side, we were lacking width,  so players were coming inside and inside. So in  
many moments we were lacking 20 metres off the  pitch and narrowing ourselves down and slowing  
ourselves down, and changing positions for too  long. It's not a problem to change positions,  
but you have to find your position again so that  everyone knows how to start the attack and then  
you can just accelerate the game easier. We were  taking a lot of crosses, a lot of long-range  
shots, which is normally not our style of play.  We played a lot of long balls. We played a lot  
of long passes. That was not part of training  in the last four days. So yeah, it was a bit of  
a mix of everything. That's why the first half  looked how it looked. Second half, like I said,  
I liked the second half more on the sideline.  You talked yesterday about how sharp Harry  
was. Did that goal show it? Yeah, that's what he  does. He's always there to score and, in the end,  
the decisive goal. Like always, no secrets there.  If you score, it helps you and gives you a bit  
more rhythm, a bit more confidence. So it's a bit  easier for the second group to start with a 1-0.  
Harry is in top shape and I think, anyway, that  when the pressure comes and the tournament starts,  
that will bring the best out of our players. You  mentioned the pitch earlier, Thomas. Obviously  
a lot was said and written about it. What did  you make of it? And has everybody come through  
okay? Yeah, it was very, very difficult to  play on. I think it was not so dangerous to  
have injuries. We have no injuries and there were  no concerns. But it was very uneven, very uneven,  
and it was difficult to move the ball and move  the ball quickly. When you have the ball for the  
majority of the match, it doesn't help you. Does  that surprise you, that you've had to deal with  
that in the first game? It is what it is. It can  happen. I know it from pre-season tours overseas,  
that this can happen if you play in stadiums that  are normally not football stadiums, that the pitch  
is maybe too new and not fully grown and not fully  even. So, part of it. How important was Jude in  
bringing the extra bite in the second half? He  was a part of it. But you can see, I think you  
can see, Jude has for sure the decisiveness and  he has the bite. This is his key characteristic.  
But you can see that he comes from an injury and  is full of energy and then happy to be back on  
the pitch. He had his break, unfortunately, in a  decisive part of the season, the Champions League  
season and national campaign for the championship  in Spain. So this was very unfortunate for Real  
Madrid and for him personally. But you can see  now that he is actually in a sweet spot. He comes  
back, he's fresh, he wants to play and he's in  top shape. Thomas, we've seen Nico O'Reilly play  
in midfield in the age group with England as well.  Obviously, you've used him a lot as a left-back.  
Where do you see him? Normally as a left-back,  but we have nine defenders for eight positions  
today and the position from Declan Rice was free.  Even if he plays left-back, he plays as a left  
eight and left 10. So yeah, we saw him many times  playing for Pep in this position and for Man City,  
so we thought maybe just do it. But he trained  the majority of the time as a left defender. I  
think both is possible. How much flexibility does  Nico O'Reilly, being able to play as an inverted  
full-back, play as a six, play as an eight as we  saw him today, and Reece James being able to tuck  
into midfield, how much does that help your squad  selection? I was just happy to see Reece back and  
fresh back in training and with confidence in  his body because you can just see out there,  
once he has his 45 minutes, he can produce special  moments any time. He has the body to defend on the  
highest level and the physicality. So it's a full  package as well. He gives us flexibility because  
he plays many times for Chelsea as a six, so he is  a candidate to play there as well. At the moment,  
he plays for us, and he played for us  in international football, as a right  
full-back. That's for me his main position for  us. But he stays an alternative in the middle  
of the pitch. Elliot is doing very well. Also for  Reece, he had his injury, unfortunately for him  
and unfortunately for Chelsea. But you can see now  he's actually also reaching kind of a sweet spot  
of excitement and hunger and joy to be back on  the pitch. I'm from Costa Rica. Why did you choose  
Costa Rica for the other game and another national  team from Central America? Why Costa Rica? What  
do you want to see? I have to be very honest, I  haven't prepared Costa Rica until today, so we  
will start with it tomorrow. So please forgive me  for that, that I'm not very well prepared for that  
in detail. We wanted to play against different  continents. We wanted to play against different  
styles and not against a European team. Costa Rica  is a football country and will bring emotions and  
will bring excitement, of course. It's a good  test for us. To adapt to a different style,  
to adapt to a different mentality were the key  reasons. We will prepare from tomorrow and then  
we have three days to be prepared and take the  next step against your country. What was your  
opinion on Ivan Toney's performance amid some  public scrutiny about his inclusion in the squad?  
Ivan was very impressive in training and he plays  a kind of special role in our team. I think he  
gives us the possibility, if we dominate and if  we have a lot of touches in and around the box,  
he gives us the chance to play with Harry, take  attention of central defenders and be strong in  
finishing and strong in set pieces. He had one big  chance today that he missed, but it was offside,  
so this let him off the hook. But he trains very  well and he's a very important team member because  
he connects with everyone. Very social and it's  good. Very happy with him until now. Thomas,  
yesterday you said there were two main focuses  today. One was minutes on the pitch and it was  
connections between two or three players.  Should we read anything into decisions with  
your centre-halves and your goalkeeper in the  first half, and then Marcus, Morgan and Harry? No,  
not too much. No, not too much. The connections  were more like, we put Morgan and Ollie together  
because they know each other. We put a  left side together with Dan Burn, Dino and  
Anthony Gordon from Newcastle so that they have  it a bit easier. But decisions are not made yet  
for Croatia and there were no hidden messages. We  tried to have more or less equal teams. Harry and  
Morgan played many matches for us together. Then  we had yesterday a strong group in training with  
Jude and Nico and Elliot Henderson, and we just  kept them together because they enjoyed playing  
together yesterday in training. So that was it.  But no secret messages behind that. Thank you.
title: TUCHEL: “I'M NOT SUPER HAPPY!”  England 1-0 New Zealand  World Cup warm-up
